items.title: Leading Analytical Techniques for Driving Informed Decision-Making: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Rationale of Study: This study reviews common analytical techniques for decision-making, analyses their applications and effectiveness, and identifies the required skills. It also explores contextual factors like interpretability, data quality, and skill gaps that hinder implementation, offering insights for practitioners and researchers. Methodology: This study reviews 27 peer-reviewed articles from 2019-2024, using PRISMA to map analytical techniques for decision-making. It shows a shift from descriptive to predictive and prescriptive analytics, mainly driven by ML and AI. The research also suggests combining automated systems with human judgment to enhance decision-making amid complex, data-rich environments. Findings: The study highlights a shift from descriptive to predictive and prescriptive analytics, driven by advances in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). To build trust and adoption, strong data governance, ongoing professional development, and clear AI model explanations are crucial. Future research should balance interpretability with real-time analytics and integrate automated systems with human judgment to enhance performance. Implications: Access to this information fosters a culture of informed decision-making. Developing data governance is vital to ensure data quality, integrity, and ethical use. Qualified professionals with industry knowledge and technical skills are in short supply. Integrating data scientists, analysts, and decision-makers requires expertise in statistics, programming, data storytelling, and strategy. The paper recommends investing in the professional growth of cross-functional analytics teams. Originality: The rapid adoption of machine learning and AI has shifted decision-making from descriptive reporting to predictive and prescriptive approaches. Extracting insights from complex datasets is now a key competitive edge.

items.title: Leakage-Controlled and Calibrated Deep Ensemble Learning for Reliable COVID-19 Classification from Chest X-Ray and CT Images
items.abstract: Reliable evaluation of artificial intelligence models for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) imaging remains challenging because patient-level dependencies, source-related biases, and differences between imaging modalities can lead to overly optimistic performance estimates. This study proposes a leakage-controlled, modality-aware deep ensemble framework for COVID-19 classification using chest X-ray (CXR) and computed tomography (CT) images from the COVID-19 Radiography Database and the SARS-CoV-2 CT-Scan Dataset. Separate evaluation protocols were established for CXR and CT, with duplicate control and available source information incorporated for CXR and patient-level partitioning applied to CT before data augmentation. Four ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs)—VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet169, and InceptionV3—were evaluated, followed by temperature scaling for probability calibration and validation-optimized weighted soft voting for ensemble fusion. The original CT architectural comparison was conducted at the slice level, whereas the final CT evaluation was performed at the patient level. In the final modality-specific held-out evaluation, DenseNet169 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.985, an accuracy of 97.32%, and an F1-score of 98.1% on the 2870-image CXR test set. The calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.990, an accuracy of 98.43%, and an F1-score of 97.9%, with a Brier score of 0.030 and an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.023. For CT, DenseNet169 achieved an AUROC of 0.941 and correctly classified 16 of 18 patients (88.89%), whereas the calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.969 and correctly classified 17 of 18 patients (94.44%), with a Brier score of 0.070 and an ECE of 0.053. An uncertainty-aware selective-prediction analysis identified 316 of 2870 CXR test images (11.01%) and 2 of 18 CT test patients (11.11%) as low-confidence cases for specialist review. Among the remaining CT cases, 15 of 16 patients were correctly classified (93.75%). Because the CT test cohort contained only 18 patients, the patient-level CT performance and selective-prediction results should be interpreted cautiously as descriptive estimates from this limited cohort. The original pooled evaluation, in which DenseNet169 achieved 98.51% accuracy, is retained only as an exploratory architectural comparison and should not be interpreted as directly comparable with the final modality-specific evaluation. The findings demonstrate that evaluation design, statistical unit, probability calibration, and ensemble fusion materially influence the interpretation of COVID-19 imaging-classification performance. The proposed framework provides leakage-aware and calibrated performance estimates under the evaluated datasets; however, independent multicenter external validation is required before broader claims of clinical generalizability or deployment readiness can be made.

items.title: Learning How to Learn
items.abstract: This chapter brings John Dewey’s account of educative experience into conversation with Meighan’s sociological analysis of control and agency in schooling, and Zimmerman’s model of self-regulated learning, to clarify what it means to “learn how to learn” across the life course. It argues that learning to learn is neither a generic skill nor an individual trait, but a set of capacities cultivated through intentionally designed experiences, clear expectations, and structured opportunities for reflection, uptake of feedback, and purposeful action. Learner agency is shaped not only by formal institutional arrangements but also by tacit classroom norms, peer dynamics, and the emotional conditions required for risk-taking and self-monitoring. This chapter also considers contemporary pressures, especially the ease of fluent artificial intelligence (AI)-generated answers that can short-circuit reflective effort unless learners are explicitly guided to plan, monitor, and evaluate their thinking. Through an integrative framework and a practical evidence map, including marginalia from practising teachers, the chapter illustrates how these ideas travel into classroom judgement. It offers design principles for educators who wish to build autonomy without abandoning structure and to support diverse learners in developing sustainable habits of inquiry, critique, and lifelong learning (LLL). It serves as a conceptual runway in teacher education and related modules.

items.title: Learning to Welcome the Answer
items.abstract: Complete illustrated English and French editions of Learning to Welcome the Answer / Apprendre à accueillir la réponse, a research essay by Jean-Sébastien Beaulieu. English abstract I examine what it means to welcome a mathematical answer produced with artificial intelligence while preserving the understanding that makes an answer useful. The article begins with my response to OpenAI's release of mathematical manuscripts and the perspective acquired through four years of work on my own project. Thirty sources guide an exploration of proof, formalization, computation, fractal geometry, classification, research provenance and digital protection. Each technical example connects a concept with its assumptions and the conditions of a possible application. The discussion then turns toward Book III with Aguilar and my preparation for NASA Space Apps. A geometric descriptor offers a concrete research question: what information would it contribute under a fair comparison? Feature addition and adaptive selection of an analysis scale remain distinct experimental proposals. Their assessment calls for defined observables, appropriate reference methods, an availability record for the data and reproducible evaluation. I place these questions within a wider concern for participation. Clear explanations, usable research materials and accessible tools help people turn curiosity into sustained work. My position is an invitation to celebrate shared knowledge through careful reading, explicit validation and practical contribution. The work invested in a question becomes part of the judgment with which a new answer is received. Résumé français J'examine ce que signifie accueillir une réponse mathématique produite avec l'intelligence artificielle tout en préservant la compréhension qui la rend utile. L'article part de ma réaction à la publication de manuscrits mathématiques par OpenAI et du regard acquis au cours de quatre années consacrées à mon propre projet. Trente sources accompagnent une exploration de la preuve, de la formalisation, du calcul, de la géométrie fractale, de la classification, de la provenance des travaux et de la protection numérique. Chaque exemple technique relie un concept à ses hypothèses et aux conditions d'une application possible. La réflexion se poursuit vers le Livre III avec Aguilar et ma préparation à NASA Space Apps. Un descripteur géométrique fournit une question de recherche concrète : quelle information apporterait-il dans une comparaison équitable ? L'ajout d'une variable et le choix adaptatif d'une échelle d'analyse demeurent deux propositions expérimentales distinctes. items.title: Lecturers’ Awareness and Attitudes Towards the Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka
items.abstract: The increasing availability of artificial intelligence (AI) tools presents new opportunities and challenges for teaching and learning in higher education. This study examined lecturers’ awareness of and attitudes towards the use of AI tools at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka. A descriptive survey design was adopted. Four research questions and two hypotheses guided the study. The population comprised academic staff in the Department of Science Education, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, from whom 49 lecturers participated in the study. Data were collected using a researcher-developed instrument titled Questionnaire on Lecturers’ Awareness Level and Attitude to AI Tools (QLALAAIT). The instrument was subjected to face validation and trial testing, and its overall reliability coefficient, determined using Cronbach’s alpha, was 0.83. Data were analysed using mean and standard deviation to answer the research questions, while analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to test the hypotheses at the 0.05 level of significance. The findings indicated that lecturers demonstrated awareness of selected AI tools, including ChatGPT, Turnitin, and QuillBot, and generally expressed positive attitudes towards their use in educational contexts. Further analysis showed that years of teaching experience did not significantly influence lecturers’ awareness of or attitudes towards AI tools. The study highlights the need for structured professional development, institutional support, and access to appropriate resources to facilitate informed and effective use of AI tools in university teaching and related academic activities.

items.title: LEGAL ISSUES OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is the challenge of the new era that has imposed its presence and intervened in various aspects of life, especially the science of law. Will the machine improve the art of drafting legal texts to control human behavior, now that its intelligence has surpassed that of humans? Have legal texts addressed such dangerous interference that has included several fields, starting from copyright and e-commerce to the point of the existence of predictive judiciary as an alternative to traditional judiciary governed by machines? Is the law really going through the digitization crisis imposed on it by reality? We are facing a new challenge, and a new legal arsenal is required to regulate its provisions and benefit from its advantages.

items.title: LensErase: A Foundation Model for Erase Anything
items.abstract: We introduce LensErase, a general-purpose mask-based Erase Anything foundation model designed to cover a broad spectrum of real-world erase scenarios. LensErase supports diverse objects, visual text, watermarks, associated visual effects, multiple-object removal, and a wide range of object scales, aspect ratios, and image resolutions. First, to enable such broad coverage, we construct LensErase-100M, a large-scale dataset containing 101.07 million paired source-mask-target examples spanning diverse erase scenarios. Second, we pretrain LensErase from the text-to-image model Lens, adapting its strong generative prior to mask-based erasing. To efficiently incorporate the source image and erase mask, we propose Mask-Aware RoPE, a 3D rotary positional encoding that directly injects mask information into the source-image tokens without introducing a separate mask token sequence. Finally, we refine the model through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with contract-guided, region-aware rewards, and apply TraceFusion at inference to preserve high-fidelity content outside the effective edit region. Across six public benchmarks and the proposed LensErase-Bench, LensErase achieves substantial improvements under both reference-based objective metrics and reference-free VLM evaluation. We hope LensErase can serve as a foundational model for erase-related applications and systems.

items.title: Liderazgo adaptativo e innovador: articulación entre innovación pedagógica y gestión estratégica en la educación superior
items.abstract: The transformation of higher education has increased the need to articulate classroom-based innovation with institutional management and governance processes. In this context, academics who assume academic program leadership responsibilities occupy an intermediate position between teaching practice and strategic management, although the literature frequently addresses these dimensions separately. This article aims to analyze and integrate recent literature on academic leadership, pedagogical innovation, governance, and faculty development in higher education, with particular attention to the role of academic middle leaders as agents connecting educational practice and institutional change. An integrative literature review was conducted based on thematic relevance, recency, scientific quality, and availability of DOI, complemented by regional evidence concerning artificial intelligence adoption and governance in Latin American and Caribbean higher education. The thematic synthesis identified four interconnected dimensions: adaptive and innovative leadership, academic middle leadership, shared governance, and servant leadership. The findings suggest that institutionalizing innovation depends not only on individual faculty initiative but also on organizational conditions that promote participation, trust, capacity development, and shared decision-making. The study concludes that academic program leaders who maintain a teaching role can become strategic actors connecting pedagogical innovation with institutional management when they have adequate autonomy, leadership development, and organizational support.

items.title: LifeSearch: Benchmarking Deep Research Agents for Real-World Life and Productivity
items.abstract: Deep research (DR) agents address open-ended information needs through multi-step reasoning, long-horizon web search, and evidence synthesis. However, existing benchmarks primarily focus on academic research or synthetic tasks, leaving DR agents' capabilities in real-world life and professional productivity settings insufficiently evaluated. To bridge this gap, we introduce LifeSearch, a challenging benchmark comprising 203 Chinese and English tasks derived from real-user query seeds across 7 concrete life and productivity domains. With more than 4,500 hours of human annotation, we construct over 4,000 expert-written, fine-grained rubrics, covering both report-content criteria for coverage and accuracy and concrete criteria specifying values, units, dates, and URLs. We conduct extensive experiments on 12 advanced DR agents under a unified evaluation harness, systematically analyzing their performance patterns and failure modes. We find that even the best-performing frontier agent, GPT-5.6 Sol, achieves a score of only 63.4%, leaving substantial room for improvement on realistic life and professional DR tasks. We select the grading configuration by comparing candidate LLM judges against human rubric labels, and a human ranking study shows strong alignment between aggregate benchmark scores and human judgments (Spearman's $ρ= 0.89$, Kendall's $τ= 0.81$). LifeSearch provides a rigorous evaluation framework and foundation for advancing DR agents toward real-world life and productivity.

items.title: Lifetime Sample Tracking (LiST): A data platform for materials science
items.abstract: The 2D Crystal Consortium Materials Innovation Platform (2DCC-MIP) is a NSF supported national user facility focused on advancing the synthesis of 2D materials, monolayers, surfaces, and interfaces. The need for the facility to organize and share data with users led to the development of an internal data management and analysis engine, the Lifetime Sample Tracking platform (LiST). This infrastructure allows the automated capture, curation, analysis, and dissemination of data ranging from experimental materials synthesis parameters and characterization to theoretical first-principles and ReaxFF molecular dynamics modeling [Nayir et al., 2D Mater. 10, 032002 (2023)]. The system currently hosts synthesis and property data (accessible via a REST API) on ∼20 000 samples produced by the 2DCC grown using a variety of techniques from bulk crystal growth to metal-organic chemical vapor deposition and molecular beam epitaxy, among others. Data used in publications can easily be grouped by the system into data packages that are given digital object identifiers for inclusion with each publication. The LiST platform is now being used by groups outside of the 2DCC as a solution for data curation in materials science. Data management tools, such as LiST, support the materials development process by allowing a closed loop iteration between synthesis, characterization, theory, and targeted materials design. This also enables machine learning research, artificial intelligence analysis, and the potential for autonomous synthesis in the future.

items.title: ListQA: A Benchmark for Evaluating List-Formatted Factual Knowledge Retrieval in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Many real-world questions demand not a single fact but an organized collection of them, yet existing factual knowledge benchmarks almost exclusively target single answer retrieval. We introduce ListQA, a benchmark of 9,045 human-curated, cross-validated questions (audited error rate of 1.7%) that require LLMs to recall multiple facts and compose them into structured lists of 3-10 elements. Questions range from flat lists ("Which NCAA teams went undefeated between 2000 and 2024?") to hierarchical lists with sub-attributes ("...and what was their record and result?"), spanning eight categories across 60+ countries. An evergreen design (explicit temporal constraints or historically immutable facts) keeps ground truth valid without periodic updates. For evaluation, we frame element matching as a linear sum assignment problem: optimal bipartite matching paired with LLM-based semantic grading jointly captures factual accuracy, hallucination, and format compliance. We benchmark 34 models (8 families, 42 configurations across standard and thinking enabled inference) and find: the best standard-inference model scores below 37% LLM-Judge-F1, multi-faceted questions are harder across the board, and providing the source Wikipedia page lifts scores dramatically, confirming that models can organize facts but struggle to retrieve them from parameters alone. Extended analyses cover base vs. instruction-tuned checkpoints and token efficiency. We release the dataset and evaluation code.

items.abstract: Evaluation for automatic crisis reporting should measure what practitioners need, not what is convenient to compare. Through LLM-assisted, author-approved content analysis, we derive a 15-slot information schema from professional humanitarian situation reports using qualitative content analysis, then evaluate 121 human and 261 LLM-generated reports across five disasters and three hazard types. Under google/gemini-3.7-flash on Cyclone Idai, the best machine arm is nominally above the empirical human ceiling (0.827 vs. 0.821), but the difference is statistically indistinguishable from zero (95\% bootstrap CI $[-.049,.059]$; permutation $p=.852$), and the ordering does not replicate under openai/gpt-5.6-luna. On a blind 100-item Idai sample, the author agrees with the Gemini judge at 0.910 accuracy and unweighted Cohen's $κ=.799$. All four judges clear the plan's raw-agreement criterion of .7; only Gemini reaches .7 on chance-corrected $κ$. Across the three primary events, machine reports reproduce 5.4-11.0% of same-day official figures. Across those same events, raw exact-number matching links 14.3-19.6% of official figures and 85.4-90.1% of machine figures to the social stream; manual audit confirms 45/50 declared absences, 4/25 official matches, and 24/25 machine matches semantically. The issuing-provenance gap is positive in all 12 observed event-judge cells: report date, organisation, series, and authority were not supplied at professional-report coverage in any cell. On the three primary events, ROUGE-L is uninformative, BERTScore is negatively associated with completeness after multiplicity correction, and a generic LLM judge changes sign.

items.title: Machine Learning on Heterogeneous, Edge, and Quantum Hardware for Particle Physics
items.abstract: The next generation of particle physics experiments will face an era of challenges in data acquisition, due to unprecedented data rates and volumes along with extreme environments and operational constraints. Harnessing these data for scientific discovery demands real-time inference and decision-making, intelligent data reduction, and efficient processing architectures beyond current capabilities. Crucial to the success of this experimental paradigm are several emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning, silicon microelectronics, and the advent of quantum algorithms and processing. Their intersection includes areas of research such as low-power and low-latency devices for edge computing, heterogeneous accelerator systems, reconfigurable hardware, codesign and synthesis strategies, readout for cryogenic or high-radiation environments, and analog computing. This white paper presents a community-driven vision to identify and prioritize research and development opportunities in hardware-based ML systems and corresponding physics applications, contributing toward a successful transition to the data frontier of fundamental science.

items.title: Machine--human agreement in marking undergraduate assignments is specific to model, prompt and institution
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) promise to automate one of higher education's most resource-intensive activities: assessing student writing. Existing evaluations are typically limited to a single model, a single prompt and a single institution. Using 761 undergraduate psychology assignments from three UK universities, we evaluated three frontier LLMs, individually and in ensemble, on accuracy, prompt sensitivity, error independence, generalisability and evidential basis. Agreement between human and machine marks varied widely, with no model or prompt optimal across institutions. All models compressed marks towards a common central tendency, overvaluing the weakest assignments and undervaluing the strongest. Because this error was shared, ensembling failed to remove it. Machine marks also rewarded linguistic features more strongly than human marks. Since human-machine agreement was a joint product of model, prompt and institution, we conclude that current LLMs lack evaluative capacity transferable across contexts, and that single-context validation overstates readiness for deployment.

items.title: Making AI-mediated decisions culturally repairable
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly influences high-stakes decisions, from employment and education to healthcare and public services. When such judgments are disputed, affected people may receive an explanation without being able to reach an authority empowered to change the outcome or remedy its consequences. We introduce cultural repairability: the institutional capacity to review an AI-mediated decision, correct the outcome and downstream records, provide meaningful restoration, and learn from failure through procedures people can understand and use. The framework addresses a visibility–accountability asymmetry: people are exposed to judgments about their standing but lack effective means of obtaining an answer or remedy. Culture matters because exposure, legitimate authority, and appropriate restoration may be understood differently across settings. Language accessibility also determines whether review mechanisms are usable in practice. We identify three measurable cultural mechanisms: the meaning of exposure, the credibility of review, and the meaning of restoration. We further distinguish affected people’s appraisals from institutional actors’ responsibility and capacity to respond. Four falsifiable propositions specify how reviewer authority and audience shape responses to repair, and how these effects vary with cultural orientation, institutional history, and the form of restoration. They predict whether people appeal or withdraw, how they recalibrate trust, and whether they remain willing to engage. The resulting Repairability Principle establishes a common floor of substantive review, correction, restoration, and prevention of recurrence, while allowing people to choose how restoration is delivered. Cultural repairability therefore shifts global AI accountability from whether procedures appear acceptable to whether institutions can correct harm in practice.

items.title: Many Right Answers, One Training Example: Removing Responder Noise from GRPO for LLM Recommenders
items.abstract: A recommendation request on Reddit draws several replies, each naming different titles. When an LLM recommender is trained on such threads with reinforcement learning (RL), which replies should a generated list be rewarded against? The state-of-the-art recipe, Rank-GRPO, picks one reply per training example, so the advantage mostly records which reply was drawn (85% of its variance) rather than how good the list is. We argue that RL should train on the request, not on each answer, and propose ReMaRk: it scores every list once against the union of all replies' titles and samples each request equally. This makes RL cheaper. On seven backbones and three datasets, ReMaRk reaches the validation recall of 2,000 per-reply RL steps in 25 to 53% of the steps and leads at that budget; trained until neither improves, it is never significantly behind Rank-GRPO and in four of seven pairs reaches Rank-GRPO's best with fewer GPU-hours. The same reward helps on ProtoQA, where about 100 people answer each question, which points to a simple rule for RL with several valid human answers: reward them jointly.

items.title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents
items.abstract: Thought templates, skill libraries, agent memories and caches turn many reasoning steps into one. We call this reasoning contraction. A contracted memory saves reasoning steps and errors until its facts change, then quietly answers wrong. Most systems trust memories by counting successes and failures. We prove that such counters are badly tuned change detectors: a symmetric counter notices a partial change only after a power of its false-alarm horizon, and an unclipped one may never notice it. On five LLMs answering multi-hop questions over edited facts, ExpeL- and ACE-style counters serve 7.0-13.5x more stale answers than certified memories given the same information, and on code tasks with an exact verifier 35-73x more. Safety also has a price. When facts change and each memory is judged only by its own verified outcomes, one number, the certification load, sets how much reasoning any safe memory can skip, and under Zipf demand it yields a scaling law. Our recipe weighs each memory's failures by its own likelihood ratio, certifies its utility against live reasoning, and restarts the certificate when facts change, with the likelihood-ratio detector as the safety net for unannounced changes; for large edits it also invalidates the memory.

items.title: Mechanisms of Brand Authenticity Erosion in AI-Generated Advertising: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in advertising since 2022 has transformed content production while raising concerns about the preservation of brand authenticity, a critical foundation of consumer trust and brand relationships. This study examines how AI-generated advertising influences perceived brand authenticity, identifies the mechanisms driving authenticity erosion, and explains the contextual factors that account for inconsistent findings in prior research. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this review synthesizes 13 studies published between 2022 and 2026 retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and EBSCOhost databases. Through thematic synthesis, this study identifies three interrelated mechanisms through which AI-generated advertising may undermine brand authenticity: disclosure effects, failed anthropomorphism, and sincerity erosion. The findings further reveal that the effects of AI-generated advertising on authenticity perceptions are contingent upon individual characteristics, product and brand contexts, and source-related factors, including AI capability beliefs, product type, luxury positioning, and communicator characteristics. This study develops an integrated framework explaining when and why AI-generated advertising enhances or undermines brand authenticity, thus providing theoretical insights for consumer research and practical implications for AI-enabled marketing decision-making.

items.title: Mechanization and Agronomic Approaches for Reducing Farm Drudgery and Labour Requirement in Agriculture: A Critical Narrative Review
items.abstract: Agricultural work remains physically demanding and strongly seasonal in many production systems, while labour scarcity, rising wages, ageing farm populations, and competing non-farm employment are increasing pressure to complete operations with less human effort. This critical narrative review evaluates how mechanization and agronomic redesign can reduce farm drudgery and labour requirement without assuming that labour saved at an individual task is equivalent to labour displaced from agriculture. Literature published from 1 January 1990 to 6 August 2026 was identified through accessible scholarly databases and indexes, supplemented by citation searching and authoritative institutional sources. Evidence was appraised for study design, measurement of labour and ergonomic outcomes, external validity, treatment of confounding, duration, and attention to gender, safety, and implementation conditions. The strongest evidence indicates that mechanization can markedly reduce time and physiological burden in power-intensive and repetitive operations, but whole-farm labour effects vary because mechanization also changes cultivated area, input intensity, timeliness, and the allocation of family and hired labour. Ergonomic hand tools and scale-appropriate machines are especially important where capital-intensive mechanization is infeasible. Agronomic approaches such as zero or reduced tillage and direct-seeded rice can remove labour-intensive operations, yet their labour-saving value is conditional on weed control, crop establishment, residue management, and access to compatible equipment. Conservation agriculture illustrates this conditionality: manual planting basins or increased hand weeding can offset labour savings, whereas mechanized establishment and effective weed management can reduce peak labour demand. Gendered task allocation, machinery access, custom hiring services, occupational safety, and rural employment transitions determine who benefits and who bears adjustment costs. Robotics and autonomous equipment may address labour shortages in selected systems, but economic feasibility, field reliability, supervision, and human-machine safety remain important constraints. The review concludes that drudgery reduction is best pursued through integrated mechanization-agronomy packages evaluated with task-specific ergonomic measures and whole-household, whole-season labour accounting.

items.title: Media neophraseologisms as a marker of transformational and innovative processes in the Russian phraseological system
items.abstract: This article is devoted to a comprehensive study of media neophraseologisms as relevant markers of transformation processes in the modern Russian phraseological system. Using extensive empirical data from the Russian-language online press and Telegram channels for 2020–2026, the article identifies key derivational trends in neophraseology: structural diffuseness, pragmemization, and sententialization of signs. We demonstrate a semantic shift in neoidioms toward de-abstraction and connection to the current agenda and substantiate the adaptive nature of phraseological innovations in the context of an increasingly complex information picture of the world. Particular attention is paid to the anthropocentric aspect of linguistic creativity: The generation of neophraseologisms, mediated by the mechanisms of irony, allusion, and manipulation, is verified as a demarcation line between the natural human text generation and the algorithms of generative artificial intelligence. We propose a typology of neophraseologisms, including discursive-precedent, intermedia, and calqued units, including their axiological and ludic functions in media texts. The article notes that the diffuseness of structure and pragmemization act as mechanisms of linguistic economy, while the de-abstraction of signs reflects the connection between phraseology and extralinguistic factors. The results are significant for lexicographic practice, university teaching, and media stylistics. The developed typology and the identified derivational processes can serve as a basis for monitoring the Russian phraseological system evolution. The results of the study are applicable in lexicographic practice, teaching, and media stylistics.

items.title: MEDICAL REHABILITATION OF MUSCULOSKELETAL DISORDER
items.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are conditions affecting the muscles, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments, cartilage, and other supporting structures of the body. They may be acute or chronic and can result from trauma, repetitive movements, poor posture, aging, genetic factors, occupational hazards, or inflammatory diseases. Common musculoskeletal disorders include osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, low back pain, tendinitis, bursitis, fractures, and muscle strains.The main symptoms are pain, swelling, stiffness, muscle weakness, restricted joint movements, and difficulty performing daily activities. Diagnosis is based on medical history, physical examination, and investigations such as X-rays, CT scans, MRI, blood tests, and bone mineral density measurements, depending on the condition.Treatment aims to relieve pain, reduce inflammation, restore mobility, and prevent disability. Management includes medications, physiotherapy, therapeutic exercises, heat and cold therapy, occupational therapy, and lifestyle modifications. In severe cases, surgical intervention may be necessary. Medical rehabilitation plays an essential role in improving muscle strength, joint flexibility, balance, coordination, and functional independence.Prevention involves maintaining correct posture, regular physical activity, a balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D, maintaining a healthy body weight, using proper workplace ergonomics, and avoiding repetitive strain. Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment help reduce complications and improve quality of life. A multidisciplinary approach involving doctors, physiotherapists, and occupational therapists is essential for effective management and long-term recovery.

items.title: MemeTrace: A Multimodal LLM-Based Agent for Safety-Aware Meme Provenance Analysis
items.abstract: Online memes are often carriers of unsafe content such as disinformation and propaganda. Their rapid evolution in response to news events and strong dependence on contextual information make it difficult for platforms and moderators to detect and moderate them effectively. Moreover, existing moderation studies typically classify memes as safe or unsafe based on individual images, lacking the ability to perform broader provenance analysis, i.e., where a meme originates, how it spreads, what cultural symbolism it represents, whether it poses potential risks to society, etc. To bridge this gap, we introduce MemeTrace, a multimodal LLM-based agent that automatically traces the provenance and potential risks of emerging memes. We evaluate MemeTrace on Meme100, a dataset of 100 real-world memes, using both human annotation and automatic metrics. The results demonstrate that MemeTrace substantially outperforms the VLM baseline. More importantly, MemeTrace achieves higher accuracy in detecting unsafe memes, especially those involving disinformation and sensitive content, and remains robust under visual perturbations.

items.title: Metaheuristic Approaches for the Satisfiability Problem (SAT): A Systematic Review and Comparative Study with Modern SAT Solvers
items.abstract: The Boolean Satisfiability Problem is a central challenge in artificial intelligence and combinatorial optimization, with applications in circuit verification, planning, and bioinformatics. This study makes two main contributions: a systematic review of metaheuristic approaches conducted under the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) protocol, and a comparative evaluation of 11 algorithms. The considered methods include genetic algorithms, genetic algorithms with stepwise adaptation of weights, hybrid grey wolf genetic algorithms, genetic-based local search, population-based simulated annealing, dynamic clause weighting local search, stochastic local search, phase transition-based local search, random walk with local (1 + 1) evolutionary algorithm, improved adaptive genetic algorithm, and artificial bee colony. The evaluation relies on multiple criteria, including solution quality, robustness, success rate with confidence intervals, computational efficiency, and scalability across the benchmark families UF20 to UF250, complemented by additional benchmarks from the SAT Challenge Random Track (2018) and newly generated random 3-SAT instances. The results show that Genetic Algorithm, phase transition-based local search, dynamic clause weighting local search, genetic-based local search, random walk with local (1+1) Evolutionary Algorithm, and Artificial Bee Colony provide the most robust performance, maintaining a balance between exploration and exploitation. Beyond comparisons within metaheuristics, the study also examines how bio-inspired approaches compare with modern SAT solvers based on conflict-driven clause learning and stochastic local search across different problem scales. By contrast, highly specialized variants, such as genetic algorithms with stepwise adaptation of weights, population-based simulated annealing, hybrid grey wolf genetic algorithms, and improved adaptive genetic algorithms, degrade significantly on larger benchmarks. Overall, this study consolidates the strengths and weaknesses of metaheuristics and outlines future directions for adaptability, hybridization with machine learning, and scalable computations.

items.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
items.abstract: Multi-objective molecular optimization is a critical process in drug discovery that aims to modify a given molecule to simultaneously improve multiple properties while maintaining a similar overall structure. This process often requires iterative modifications guided by computational or experimental feedback. Recent large language model (LLM)-based methods have begun to explore this iterative approach; however, these methods are not explicitly trained to leverage such feedback, while existing approaches primarily focus on single-turn molecular optimization. To address this gap, we introduce Multi-turn Feedback Guided (MFG) molecular optimization, a reinforcement learning framework that trains an LLM to progressively optimize molecules using feedback from previous turns. MFG introduces a feedback vector capturing both property improvements and source molecule similarity, alongside a feedback-aligned reward function that promotes progressive improvement across turns. We apply MFG over $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$, a state-of-the-art LLM model for multi-objective molecular optimization, evaluate $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ on ten multi-objective molecular optimization tasks. The results demonstrate that $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ achieves the highest average similarity-constrained success rate ($81.50%$), outperforming the base model $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$ ($70.81%$).

items.abstract: Microfluidics has emerged as an important platform for manipulating and analyzing small volumes of fluids, cells, biomolecules, and particles with high precision. Its ability to control microscale flows and integrate multiple analytical steps has enabled diverse biomedical technologies, including lab-on-a-chip, point-of-care diagnostics, organ-on-chip, and microphysiological systems. This review summarizes the fundamental principles of biomedical microfluidics, including microscale fluid dynamics, laminar flow, diffusion, and key dimensionless parameters, together with major platform formats such as continuous-flow, droplet-based, and digital microfluidics. Recent fabrication approaches, including photolithography, soft lithography, molding, laser-based methods, 3D printing, micromilling, and paper- and lamination-based techniques, are also discussed. The review highlights applications in cancer and liquid biopsy, infectious disease diagnostics, cardiovascular and neurological disorders, organ-on-chip models, drug screening and toxicity testing, pharmaceutical synthesis, drug delivery, single-cell analysis, and regenerative and reproductive medicine. Particular attention is given to the growing use of microfluidics for personalized and human-relevant biomedical research. The review further examines the major challenges associated with microfluidic biomedical systems, including fabrication reproducibility, material compatibility, biological complexity, standardization, scalability and manufacturing, clinical validation, regulatory requirements, and integration with advanced computational approaches such as artificial intelligence and machine learning. Finally, future perspectives are discussed, with particular emphasis on personalized medicine, decentralized diagnostics, human-relevant drug development, multi-organ microphysiological systems, wearable and implantable microfluidics, and automated biomedical platforms.

items.title: MiND: Minimal Deterministic Middleware for Auditable Large Language Model Interactions
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in research software, yet many integrations preserve only the visible prompt and answer while losing structured evidence about configuration, provider metadata, timing, failures, and the exact request procedure. MiND is an open-source, provider-neutral middleware that places a small audit boundary between an application and an LLM. For each attempted interaction it normalizes the input, constructs an explicit request, invokes a provider adapter, normalizes the result, and stores a versioned Cycle Artifact containing the observable execution context. The same core is available through a Python API, command-line interface, local HTTP API, and a self-contained Windows interface. MiND is deliberately non-agentic: it does not infer human intention, expose hidden model reasoning, or claim deterministic repetition of stochastic model output. Its purpose is narrower—to make the surrounding execution procedure inspectable and reusable.

items.title: Mitigating Domain Shift and Dataset Bias in Deep Learning Models for Cancer Diagnostics
items.abstract: Abstract The translation of deep learning architectures from controlled experimental settings into real-world cancer diagnostics is heavily bottlenecked by domain shift and demographic bias. While models routinely achieve near-perfect retrospective performance on internal datasets, validation across external multicenter cohorts incurs a systemic and severe performance degradation, with an average metric drop of 0.16 AUC. This review provides a comprehensive metasynthesis of contemporary algorithmic mitigation paradigms designed to alleviate distribution discrepancies, evaluating techniques ranging from classical stain normalization and adversarial feature alignment to test-time adaptation and large-scale self-supervised pathology foundation models. Our analysis reveals a critical dichotomy between raw diagnostic performance and algorithmic equity: current optimization frameworks that successfully elevate aggregate macro metrics frequently do so by obscuring or actively exacerbating underlying demographic and subpopulation disparities. To achieve safe, equitable, and universally reliable clinical artificial intelligence, the field must transcend static validation habits. We outline a future roadmap anchored on three critical axes: establishing intersectional disparity indices as primary regulatory endpoints, standardizing multivendor metadata-rich benchmarks, and prioritizing.

items.title: MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision
items.abstract: Time-series analysis is increasingly studied in multimodal settings, yet most benchmarks pair temporal signals with text or with visualizations derived from the same signal. This leaves open whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate time series with real-world visual evidence. We introduce MMTA (multimodal temporal analysis), a benchmark of tri-modal tasks with diverse cross-modal complementarity patterns among time series, text, and vision. MMTA spans nine domains -- robotics, autonomous driving, human action, manufacturing, AR assistance, healthcare, recommendation, finance, and climate -- under video+TS and image+TS layouts, with a 3,524-sample test split covering classification and forecasting. The benchmark standardizes heterogeneous real-world sources into a shared schema with domain-specific prompts, provenance documentation, and success-weighted metrics that penalize both wrong answers and failed generations. Evaluating eight open-source and proprietary MLLMs reveals a shared bottleneck: representing time series as text creates very long token sequences and weakens fine-grained alignment with visual evidence, especially in long-video settings. We then introduce TimeOmni-v, a multimodal LLM extension with a dedicated time-series encoder, temporal positional alignment, modality-aware token layout, and a forecasting head. TimeOmni-v improves long-video classification and time-series inference efficiency, showing that MMTA not only exposes representation and grounding failures but also motivates targeted model design.

items.title: Mobilising AI Capability for Sustainable Supply‐Chain Transformation: The Mediating Role of Green Lean Six Sigma
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) capability can be mobilised as a strategic organisational capability for sustainable supply‐chain transformation. Integrating the Natural Resource‐Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Sociotechnical Systems Theory, the study argues that AI‐enabled sensing and decision support do not automatically translate into sustainability outcomes; strategic value emerges when technological resources, managerial competencies, human expertise and process routines are aligned. Green Lean Six Sigma (GLSS) is therefore conceptualised as an organisational architecture that converts AI‐generated insight into disciplined problem definition, waste and variation reduction, process redesign, standardisation and continuous improvement. Survey data from 361 managers and executives in supply‐chain‐intensive organisations across multiple Southeast Asian countries and sectors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. AI capability is positively associated with GLSS implementation, whereas GLSS is positively associated with environmental, economic and social supply‐chain performance. Significant indirect effects further show that GLSS acts as the transmission mechanism linking AI capability to all three triple‐bottom‐line outcomes. Because the estimated structural model did not include direct AI capability‐to‐performance paths, the evidence is interpreted as support for indirect effects rather than as proof of partial mediation. The study contributes to business strategy and sustainability research by explaining how an AI capability becomes strategically valuable when embedded in a sociotechnical improvement architecture. It also offers a staged managerial road map for harmonising AI investment, GLSS techniques and sustainable business transformation.

items.title: Modelling Risk Factors of Urban Gas Accidents for Enhanced Energy Security: An Association Rule Mining Approach Integrating Causality Theory, 24‐Model, and HFACS
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Urban gas systems are core components of global energy infrastructure, underpinning residential, commercial, and industrial energy supply while supporting low‐carbon goals. However, the growing frequency of urban gas accidents—from pipeline leaks to explosions—poses severe threats to energy security, public safety, and sustainable urban development, largely due to insufficient systematic analysis of root causes. This study addresses this gap by integrating accident causality theory, the 24‐Model, and the Human Factor Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) to investigate 100 urban gas accidents, combining Chinese (2014–2023) and global datasets. Using Apriori‐based Association Rule Mining (ARM), we identified 9 key risk factors, 19 critical association rules, and a universal causal chain, with institutional negligence (inadequate regulatory frameworks and weak supervision) confirmed as the predominant root cause. The key causal chain is: “lack of targeted energy safety regulations → poor supervision of gas infrastructure → unaddressed safety hazards → equipment failure in delivery systems → gas leakage (and subsequent ignition) → accident occurrence.” To mitigate these risks, we propose three actionable strategies: tailored safety regulations for urban gas networks, AI‐enhanced real‐time supervision systems, and competency‐based training programs. These insights not only optimize the resilience of China's gas energy systems but also provide a transferable framework for global urban energy safety management, aligning with goals for secure and sustainable urban energy.

items.title: MONITORING STUDENTS' LEARNING OUTCOMES AND ASSESSING INDIVIDUAL DEVELOPMENT WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN A DIGITAL EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT
items.abstract: This paper provides a scientific and methodological analysis of monitoring students' learning outcomes and assessing their individual development with artificial intelligence (AI) in a digital educational environment. It examines the content of learning outcome monitoring, the components on which it relies (data sources, indicators, analytical methods and feedback), and the opportunities offered by AI-based learning analytics. It also defines three groups of criteria for assessing individual development: the dynamics of results, the achievement of learning goals, and independent work and reflection. As a result, a six-stage methodology is proposed in which the teacher keeps the final pedagogical decision. The methodology is intended to support the timely and individualised assessment of students in higher education institutions.

items.title: Motivation matters in the anesthesia workforce: intrinsic and extrinsic work motivation and burnout among anesthesia staff in Karbala, Iraq
items.abstract: Healthcare professionals in anesthesia and perioperative care face sustained occupational stress, yet little is known about how motivational orientation is associated with burnout vulnerability, particularly in conflict-affected, low-resource health systems. This study examined intrinsic and extrinsic work motivation in relation to personal, work-related, and client-related burnout among anesthesia staff in Karbala, Iraq, and tested whether motivational orientation explained variance beyond demographic and occupational characteristics. A cross-sectional design was employed. A convenience sample of 150 anesthesia staff was recruited from five public and teaching hospitals in Karbala, Iraq (September–December 2025). Participants completed Arabic versions of the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI) and Work Preference Inventory (WPI), alongside a demographic-occupational questionnaire. Hierarchical multiple regression analyses tested whether intrinsic and extrinsic motivation each explained incremental variance in burnout beyond covariates, and a combined model estimated their mutual (unique) contributions. Intrinsic motivation (M = 3.82, SD = 0.62) was negatively correlated with personal (ρ = −0.48), work-related (ρ = −0.19), and client-related burnout (ρ = −0.63). Extrinsic motivation (M = 3.23, SD = 0.61) was negatively correlated with personal (ρ = −0.31) and client-related burnout (ρ = −0.56) but not with work-related burnout (ρ = −0.11, p > 0.05); the two motivation scales were strongly intercorrelated (ρ = 0.84). After accounting for covariates, intrinsic motivation explained significant additional variance in personal (ΔR² = 0.209), work-related (ΔR² = 0.053), and client-related burnout (ΔR² = 0.416; all p < 0.01). Extrinsic motivation contributed significant incremental variance to personal and client-related burnout, though less strongly, and was not a significant predictor of work-related burnout ( p = 0.146). Demographic and occupational covariates accounted for minimal variance across all models. When both scales were entered together, intrinsic motivation remained a significant negative predictor of all three burnout dimensions, whereas extrinsic motivation became a significant positive predictor of personal and work-related burnout and was unrelated to client-related burnout (Table 3). In separate models, both intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, particularly intrinsic, were associated with lower burnout among anesthesia staff in a resource-constrained, conflict-affected setting (Karbala, Iraq). After mutual adjustment, only intrinsic motivation was consistently associated with lower burnout, whereas extrinsic motivation showed a positive association with personal and work-related burnout. Although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, these findings describe associations only, and longitudinal or interventional research is needed to determine whether strengthening motivation could contribute to staff well-being strategies in similarly high-pressure environments. items.title: Multi-level point cloud transform regression via overlapping region prediction
items.abstract: Accurate and efficient point cloud registration is an important application of artificial intelligence for precise navigation and reliable decision-making in autonomous driving. However, the down-sampling of point clouds introduces interference from non-overlapping regions, resulting in the loss of important geometric information and a reduction in registration accuracy. Therefore, this study proposes an overlap-aware multi-level transformation regression network (OMTRNet), a deep-learning model that couples overlap prediction with frequency-domain and spatial feature interaction. Through a hierarchical feature extraction module designed with pixel grid mapping, we leverage the structural characteristics of pixel grids to efficiently extract point cloud features across multiple scales. By using a convolutional neural network-based overlap region prediction module, the overlap between the source and target point clouds at different scales is predicted. The overlapping region of the point cloud features is extracted from the predicted overlap, allowing for further feature extraction. Additionally, a frequency-domain feature interaction module is introduced to combine low-frequency global structural information with high-frequency local details as complementary cues for transformation estimation. Experimental results on the KITTI and NuScenes datasets validate the effectiveness of OMTRNet for large-scale partially overlapping point cloud registration. On the KITTI dataset, OMTRNet achieves an RTE of 0.2675 m, an RRE of 0.5342 deg, and a registration recall of 92.10%. The ablation results show that the DCT-based frequency-spatial interaction achieves competitive registration performance among the compared feature-interaction strategies.

items.title: Multi-System Cognitive Steering for Generative Communication
items.abstract: A fundamental bottleneck for translating thoughts to speech is the high physical cost of motor input forcing a strict tradeoff between communication speed and expressivity. Generative AI offers a promising solution by expanding highly abbreviated text input into fluent sentences, significantly reducing the motor burden on the user. However, sparse inputs are inherently ambiguous; without sufficient context, AI models frequently misinterpret these abbreviations and generate outputs that fail to align with the user's true cognitive intent. We propose \textit{Cognitive Steering}, a framework that can be leveraged to reconstruct user intent by grounding Large Language Models (LLMs) in multimodal context and applying AI control methods. We demonstrate that aligning frontier models with selected environmental referents, emotional states, and communication motives on simulated abbreviation benchmarks achieves up to $\sim$88\% top-5 expansion accuracy, doubling no-context baselines. We also reveal that different types of context require distinct AI control techniques: while physical objects in a scene are best provided through explicit text prompts, abstract factors like emotion may be more effectively managed by directly altering the AI's internal activations. These findings suggest a hybrid architecture for future interfaces that leverage Cognitive Steering to help users communicate both quickly and accurately, recruiting multiple AI control methods simultaneously to perfectly capture their intended communication goals.

items.title: Multimodal Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models in Embodied AI and Robotic Manipulation: Architectures, Cross-Embodiment Generalization, and Closed-Loop Latency Bounds
items.abstract: Abstract—Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) and autonomous robotic manipulation are undergoing an architectural paradigm shift from narrow, task-specific behavioral cloning policies toward generalist Multimodal Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models. Pre-trained on Internet-scale vision-language corpora and fine-tuned across multi-robot demonstration datasets (e.g., Open X-Embodiment), VLA models—exemplified by RT-2, Octo, and OpenVLA—perceive high-resolution RGB-D sensor streams, process unstructured natural language instructions, and autoregressively predict or diffuse continuous 7-DoF robotic end-effector trajectories. However, translating disembodied multimodal foundation models into physical cyber-physical control fabrics introduces profound physical and computational bottlenecks: continuous action space tokenization discretization errors, severe cross-embodiment kinematic domain shifts across diverse robotic morphologies, closed-loop dynamic instability induced by non-deterministic neural inference latencies (>100 ms), and safety-critical execution failure modes. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of VLA models for robotic manipulation. We formalize the Markov Decision Process (MDP) bridging autoregressive tokenization with continuous trajectory diffusion policies, model cross-embodiment action normalization across disparate robotic arm kinematics, and derive Lyapunov-Krasovskii stability bounds under stochastic computational transport delays. Furthermore, we construct an empirical robotic evaluation testbed across physical Franka Emika Panda and simulated robotic workcells evaluating 600 complex manipulation trials spanning multi-stage semantic reasoning, spatial tool use, and long-horizon pick-and-place tasks. Our empirical findings demonstrate that continuous diffusion-policy action chunking achieves an 84.6% task success rate, outperforming discrete tokenization by 28.2% while reducing kinematic jerk by 62.4%. Concurrently, asynchronous visual-action decoupling bounds closed-loop inference latency within a deterministic 20 Hz control cycle. Finally, we formulate open research directions in tactile-integrated multi-modal perception, formal barrier certificates for physical safety, and self-supervised real-world policy refinement. items.abstract: Ikisiri Utafiti huu ulilenga kuchunguza mchango wa emoji katika ujenzi na ufasiri wa maana za kipragmatiki katika diskosi za kidijitali za Kiswahili. Ingawa matumizi ya emoji yameongezeka katika mawasiliano ya mitandao ya kijamii, bado haijaelezwa kwa makini namna emoji zinavyoashiria msimamo wa mwasilishaji, kuimarisha kauli, kupunguza au kuongeza utata na kutekeleza matendo ya usemi kwa kuzingatia muktadha na dhamira ya mtumaji. Utafiti uliongozwa na Nadharia ya Umuhimu ya Sperber na Wilson (1995) na kutumia muundo wa kimaelezo. Data kuu zilijumuisha emoji 285 za aina 11 zilizokusanywa kimakusudi kutoka katika diskosi za Kiswahili kwenye WhatsApp na X. Aidha, washiriki 50 waliteuliwa kimakusudi ili kufasiri na kuthibitisha maana za emoji kulingana na muktadha. Data za ziada zilikusanywa kwa kutumia dodoso, mahojiano na majadiliano ya makundi lengwa. Emoji 285 zilitumika katika uchanganuzi mkuu, huku maoni ya washiriki yakisaidia ufasiri wake. Data zilichanganuliwa na kuwasilishwa kwa njia ya maelezo. Matokeo yalionyesha kuwa maana za emoji hujengwa kupitia mwingiliano wa vipengele vya kiisimu, kiutamaduni, kisemiotiki, kiteknolojia na kimwingiliano. Emoji zilibainika kuashiria mtazamo na dhamira ya mwasilishaji, kuimarisha au kurekebisha nguvu ya kauli, kutekeleza matendo ya usemi na kuelekeza ufasiri kulingana na muktadha. Utafiti huu unachangia uelewa wa emoji kama rasilimali za kipragmatiki na kutoa msingi wa tafiti zijazo kuhusu uchakataji wa lugha asilia kwa kutumia akili unde na maendeleo ya lugha za Kiafrika katika teknolojia ya kisasa. AbstractThis study examined the contribution of emojis to the construction and interpretation of pragmatic meaning in digital Kiswahili discourse. Although emoji use has increased in social media communication, insufficient attention has been given to how emojis signal the communicator’s stance, reinforce utterances, reduce or increase ambiguity, and perform speech acts in relation to context and the sender’s intention. The study was guided by Sperber and Wilson’s (1995) Relevance Theory and adopted a descriptive design. The main data comprised 285 emojis from 11 categories, purposively collected from Kiswahili discourse on WhatsApp and X. In addition, 50 participants were purposively selected to interpret and validate emoji meanings in context. Supplementary data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, and focus group discussions. The 285 emojis formed the primary data for analysis, while participants’ views supported their interpretation. Data were analysed and presented descriptively. The findings showed that emoji meanings are constructed through the interaction of linguistic, cultural, semiotic, technological, and interactional factors. Emojis were found to signal the communicator’s stance and intention, reinforce or modify the force of utterances, perform speech acts, and guide interpretation according to context. This study contributes to understanding emojis as pragmatic resources and provides a foundation for future research on natural language processing using artificial intelligence and the advancement of African languages in modern technology.

items.title: Narrative Lookahead in LLMs: Event-Level Decodability, Predictive Advantage, and Steering
items.abstract: Do language models carry information about narrative events before writing them, and how far ahead? We examine narrative lookahead through salient, state-changing events rather than tokens or response-level attributes. We extract 23,355 LLM-annotated events from 2,000 stories generated by four open-weight LLMs, labeling them along three nonexclusive dimensions of change: within agents, between agents, and in the story world, with human validation on a subset. Event segmentation and plot-independent labels enable comparisons across stories at horizons measured in events rather than in tokens. At event ends, we probe hidden states for upcoming event types and compare predictions with text-only predictors using matched prefixes. Across four models, future event types are decodable above prevalence baselines for at least four subsequent events, but probes significantly outperform both primary text-only predictors only for the next event. In exploratory steering with OLMo-3.1-32B, a probe-derived direction shifts the proportion of the target event type in both intended directions at higher strengths. Our event-level approach links the prediction of future narrative developments to interventions that reshape subsequent event composition.

items.title: Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence: Integrating Large Language Models with SMT Solvers, Knowledge Graphs, and Formal Automated Theorem Provers
items.abstract: Abstract—Modern deep neural networks, particularly autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs), have achieved state-of-the-art empirical performance across natural language generation, semantic translation, and broad pattern recognition. However, pure statistical connectionist architectures suffer from fundamental epistemological limitations: ungrounded factual hallucinations, an inability to guarantee mathematical soundness across multi-step deduction, brittle out-of-distribution reasoning, and a complete lack of formal explainability. Conversely, classical symbolic Artificial Intelligence (AI)—encompassing Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solvers, formal interactive theorem provers (e.g., Lean 4, Coq, Isabelle), and first-order ontological Knowledge Graphs—provides deterministic logical rigor, provable soundness, and certified safety verification, yet struggles with ambiguous perceptual inputs, continuous representations, and combinatorial state space explosion. Neuro-Symbolic AI establishes a transformative synthesis uniting statistical neural learning with rigorous symbolic reasoning. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical survey and empirical benchmark of neuro-symbolic systems across three mission-critical domains: automated mathematical olympiad proving, certified software verification, and high-stakes autonomous policy execution. We formalize differentiable fuzzy logic t-norm relaxations, model neural-guided proof search over formal tactic trees, and evaluate verified feedback loops using SMT counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR). Furthermore, we construct an empirical evaluation testbed across 1,000 rigorous verification problems spanning the miniF2F formal mathematics benchmark, SMT-LIB program assertions, and complex multi-hop knowledge graphs. Our empirical findings demonstrate that neuro-symbolic integration elevates formal Lean 4 theorem proving success from 28.4% (pure LLM sampling) to 64.2% while guaranteeing 100% mathematical soundness. Concurrently, SMT-guided neural code repair eliminates 94.6% of verified runtime invariant violations. Finally, we formulate open challenges in end-to-end differentiable symbolic unification, scalable bidirectional semantic parsing, and certified neuro-symbolic alignment. Index Terms—Neuro-Symbolic AI, Automated Theorem Proving, Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT), Lean 4, Formal Verification, Knowledge Graphs, Differentiable Logic, Proof Search.

items.title: Neuro-Symbolic Task Allocation for Heterogeneous Warehouse Robots with Versioned Knowledge Updates
items.abstract: Dynamic warehouse task allocation must coordinate loading, transport and unloading robots under changing conditions. We propose a versioned neuro-symbolic architecture in which DeepSeek proposes facts and restricted rules, an authenticated semantic shield validates them, and a mivar-inspired knowledge layer supports deterministic allocation. Stage A selects bounded dispatch candidates using CP-SAT; Stage B performs conflict-aware route and unloading-service search. The service graph supports single-carrier, abstract coalition and same-origin batch transport. Frozen evaluation separates allocation (1800 simulation runs), grounding (6102 responses) and cached-DeepSeek effects (60 episodes). Equal-map-family semantic exactness was 99.52% for facts and 93.02% for rules, but only 69.53% for moving-congestion rules. Cached restricted rules met prespecified simulator-level non-inferiority criteria for deadline misses, distance and a distance-based energy proxy. An additional 150 exploratory episodes evaluate candidate size, early unloading-robot selection, semantic shielding and emulated asynchronous integration. A separately frozen test issued 1248 new API requests on 416 synthetic events. With the contemporaneous backend, revised prompting achieved 320/320 correct congestion transactions versus 317/320 with the original prompt, without significant template-level superiority (Holm-adjusted p = 0.50). Typed-field compilation also reached 320/320 but failed validation on 10/32 access-restriction events. Complete trusted structured inputs do not require an LLM. The contribution is an auditable, bounded semantic interface; physical-robot safety, live-network reliability and physical-energy benefits remain unvalidated.

items.title: New Competencies for the Digital Doctor
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping clinical medicine, requiring physicians to develop competencies that extend beyond traditional biomedical expertise into data literacy, algorithm interpretation, prompt design, and interdisciplinary collaboration with technical teams. As predictive models increasingly influence diagnosis, treatment planning, and healthcare system operations, clinicians must understand how algorithms are trained, validated, and deployed, as well as how to recognize bias, uncertainty, and performance limitations. This chapter outlines a progressive framework of expertise ranging from basic clinical users of AI tools to clinician-scientists and clinician-engineers who co-design and evaluate intelligent health systems. It examines how digital professionalism, ethical stewardship, regulatory awareness, and patient communication must evolve in parallel with technical capability. Ultimately, the digital doctor is not defined by programming proficiency but by the ability to interpret machine-generated insight responsibly and integrate it with human judgment to ensure that artificial intelligence strengthens equitable, safe, and patient-centered care.

items.title: Nine Fallacies of Professional AI Usage: An Evidence-Based Synthesis
items.abstract: Organizations are adopting generative AI and AI decision support in professional work while evidence on their effects is still accumulating. Empirical studies document substantial productivity gains in some settings and losses in others, and practitioners carry assumptions formed during early use into everyday professional work. Research on the resulting problems is spread across human factors, human-computer interaction, fairness research, empirical economics and law, and no consolidated framework for professional use was found. This paper proposes such a framework. Its format is inspired by the Fallacies of Distributed Computing, a short list of false assumptions well known in software engineering; its content is specific to professional AI usage. Through an integrative review of peer-reviewed studies, randomized and preregistered trials, court decisions, provider documentation and regulation, nine fallacies are derived: (1) the output is correct; (2) capability is uniform across tasks; (3) the human reviewer is a reliable safeguard; (4) perceived productivity equals actual productivity; (5) AI removes work; (6) accountability moves to the tool or vendor; (7) skills and system understanding stay intact when work is delegated; (8) results transfer from benchmarks and pilots; and (9) the model is available. For each fallacy, the paper explains why the assumption persists, presents the evidence against it, states the conditions under which it does hold, and grades the strength of the evidence. It then analyzes how fallacies can compound, with particular attention to agent-built software systems that may become difficult to maintain when AI access is lost. The paper closes with implications for practice, a research agenda and a self-assessment instrument.

items.title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
items.abstract: The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. By tracking the loss distribution via an exponential moving average, this unsupervised method identifies outliers throughout a single training run. We show that this approach prevents overfitting and matches the performance of iterative refinement baselines with significantly reduced overhead. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated by recovering accurate physical observables for liquid water from unconverged reference data, including diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, we validate its scalability by training a foundation model for organic chemistry on the SPICE dataset, where it reduces both energy and force errors. This framework provides a simple, automated solution for training robust models on imperfect datasets across dataset sizes.
